newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Macronix gets big foreign orders.
newsitem.headline: Macronix gets big foreign orders.

text.p: Taiwan semiconductor maker Macronix International Co said on Monday it had received several big foreign orders worth hundreds of millions of U.S. dollars.

Some of the orders came from several major firms in Europe, Japan and the United States -- including Hewlett-Packard and Philips, Macronix administrative director Lin Yun-lung told Reuters by telephone.
"Demand for our products has risen significantly recently, and we had just received several foreign orders worth hundreds of millions of U.S. dollars," Lin said.
"These orders will last for several years, and we will start to deliver products for these orders from the third or fourth quarter (of 1997)," he said.
Lin said the total value of the orders logged had already exceeded US$100 million more than company expectations.
Macronix has set a 1997 sales target of T$13 billion, up from 1996 sales of T$10.2 billion, he said.
Boosted by news of the orders, Macronix shares soared by the daily seven percent limit to T$65.5 at close on Taiwan's stock market. ($1 = T$27.9) -- Taipei newsroom (5080815)
